thread:
priya: Quick idea — propose a "budget-safe fallthrough" feature for routing. goal: automatically route eligible low-tier requests to cheaper model variants once a per-request or per-session token-cost threshold is hit. want opinions on API shape + console UX + telemetry.

mike: sgtm. Core question: is this a per-route policy (configured by product) or a per-customer setting? both have tradeoffs. API-wise I was thinking add a routing policy like `fallthrough: { type: \"cost_cap\", thresholds: [...], fallback_model: \"...\" }`

ashley: UX note — console needs to make fallbacks visible in traces and billing. customers will freak if quality drops without an obvious signal. simplest would be a per-route toggle + explanation and a live meter showing % routed to cheaper variant.

eva: agree on visibility. also need quality gating: only fallthrough if last-N evals on that route show acceptably small delta in rouge/semantic-sim. otherwise it should fail closed. pseudo-rule: 
```
if (cost_expected > budget_threshold && quality_ok(route, fallback)) {
  route_to(fallback)
} else {
  normal_route()
}
```

sam: telemetry changes: add `route_variant_histogram(route)` and `cost_per_request` + `quality_delta_rolling` metrics. we should also emit an event when a request was fallthrough-routed so audits + support can filter.

priya: for API semantics: i'd like minimal surface for customers. maybe server-side default policy set by plan tier (free/standard/pro) but admins can override per-route. so default is opt-in on low tiers. open question: token accounting — should we consume tokens from the same quota when fallback is used or from a separate cheaper bucket?

mike: my preference: always deduct from the same token quota so users see consistent usage math. but we expose `cost_saved` in telemetry so billing can show breakdown. separate buckets complicate quota plumbing a lot.

ashley: rollout UX — which percentages? do we allow canary % for fallback? e.g., start with 5% of low-tier traffic, monitor quality delta and cost-savings, then escalate. console should surface a suggested escalation path based on telemetry.

eva: +1 for canary. also require an automatic rollback trigger: if quality_delta > X or latency regresses by Y for > N minutes then rollback fallback.

priya: sounds like we need API fields: `enabled`, `fallback_model`, `cost_threshold`, `canary_pct`, `quality_guardrails: { delta: 0.02, window_mins: 30 }`. i'll draft a design doc. who wants to own console mocks + telemetry schema?

ashley: i'll take console mocks. will add a mock of the new per-route panel and the live meter + recommended escalation buttons.

sam: i'll own telemetry + events. will sketch the metric names and the tagset (route, customer_tier, model_variant, fallback_reason).

mike: i'll prototype the API changes and a tiny server-side evaluator for the cost check. can we aim for a lightweight alpha behind a feature flag?

deploy-bot: build 3.14.7 for eng-platform merged to feature/budget-fallthrough — CI passed :white_check_mark:

priya: awesome. i'll create a doc in /docs/roadmap and link to console mock + metrics draft. lets plan a 2-week spike: API + telemetry + console mock, then sync for canary plan. thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
